content:
Sean Gallagher: Draft alert policy for perf-canary regressions (latency + throughput). Would love eyes from Runtime/Obs folks before we wire to PD.

Sean Gallagher: Goals:
- catch “real” p95 latency/tokens/sec regressions early
- don’t page ourselves into oblivion
- dedup so we don’t get 30 alerts for the same runtime deploy

Sean Gallagher: Proposed signals (per model + region + gpu_sku slice, canary traffic only, source=perf-canary):
1) p95_latency_ms regression vs baseline
2) tokens_per_sec regression vs baseline
Baseline: rolling 7d median (per ADR draft) w/ deploy-window suppression

Sean Gallagher: Thresholds v0 (paging):
- PAGE (sev2): p95 latency +25% for 20m AND min_samples >= 250 in window
- PAGE (sev2): tokens/sec -20% for 20m AND min_samples >= 250
- TICKET (sev3): p95 latency +15% for 60m (min_samples >= 500)
- TICKET (sev3): tokens/sec -10% for 60m (min_samples >= 500)

Sean Gallagher: Dedup key suggestion: {model, region, gpu_sku, metric, direction}. Not including runtime_build in dedup so we don’t explode. Alert payload should include runtime_build + last deploy SHA though.

Sean Gallagher: Suppression:
- auto-suppress 25m after runtime deploy annotation in that region
- suppress known maintenance windows (SRE calendar)

Sean Gallagher: Ask: are these thresholds too aggressive? esp for tokens/sec given batching variance.

Tomáš Novák: :eyes: thanks. I like the two-tier (page vs ticket). Concern: 20m is still short if the canary has warmup/cache priming cycles. Are we confident the canary runner is stable enough to page at +25% in 20m?

Nadia Rahman: +1 on warmup. In metrics spec draft we had “ignore first 5 minutes after canary start” but not “after deploy”. Deploy suppression helps, but if canary rotates nodes (GPU pool churn) we can still get transient spikes.

Rafael Mendes: From PD hygiene side: sev2 pages should be rare. If we page on every minor kernel tweak during rollout we’ll lose trust fast.

Allison Grant: On label schema: {model, region, gpu_sku} is ok. Please don’t add scheduler_mode into the primary alert grouping. That’s a debugging dimension, not an alert dimension, otherwise cardinality climbs.

Logan Wright: For tokens/sec specifically, we’ve seen canary variance tied to batch composition. If we page at -20% we need to ensure we’re computing tokens/sec consistently for streaming vs non-streaming (first-token alignment). Otherwise false positives.

Noah Patel: On the Runtime side: +25% p95 sustained 20m is pretty meaningful if canary is pinned scheduler + consistent prompt shapes. That said, there’s still “fleet noisy neighbor” events that can hit p95 briefly.

Sofia Ivanova: If scheduler pinning is on for canary (disable heuristic X), tokens/sec should be *more* stable than p95. p95 gets hammered by occasional queueing.

Tomáš Novák: Suggestion: require BOTH (a) regression magnitude and (b) “signal quality” gate.
Example: page only if min_samples met AND p95 of queue_wait_ms hasn’t increased >2x. Otherwise route to ticket (likely contention, not runtime regression).

Allison Grant: Careful: queue_wait_ms is a different pipeline and not always labeled the same slices. We risk paging on missing data or mismatched labels.

Sean Gallagher: good point. I’d prefer gates that are available on the exact same series.

Nadia Rahman: We can gate on “canary_success_rate” and “missing_label_count” though. If labels drop (gpu_sku missing), alert should probably be suppressed + open a telemetry bug.

Logan Wright: +1. We should include a “no data / label drop” detector separately. Perf regression alerts shouldn’t fire when the series is half-formed.

Rafael Mendes: Re: deploy suppression 25m — is that enough? Runtime rollouts sometimes take 45m region-wide depending on capacity.

Noah Patel: Our typical us-east runtime rollout is 30-40m for full saturation. But canary might be hitting a subset of nodes; suppression keyed on annotation might not cover stragglers.

Sean Gallagher: Option: suppression window = max(25m, rollout_duration_annotation). Do we have rollout duration available in deploy metadata?

Allison Grant: Release engineering doc says deploy annotation includes start_ts + end_ts (when rollout completes). If we have end_ts, we can suppress until end_ts + 10m.

Tomáš Novák: That would reduce false positives a lot.

Marissa Cole: Jumping in — from Rollouts side we *want* to detect regressions during rollout, but we don’t want to page until we’re sure it’s not warmup. Could we do: during deploy window -> ticket-only; post-deploy -> paging enabled.

Sean Gallagher: I like that. “ticket-only mode during rollout” sounds sane.

Rafael Mendes: Works operationally too. PD gets pages only when the deploy has settled.

Sean Gallagher: Updated proposal:
- If deploy annotation active for region/runtime: only open sev3 ticket alerts (no paging)
- Once deploy marked complete: enable sev2 paging after +10m buffer

Logan Wright: For tokens/sec thresholds, I’d vote -25% for paging initially, then ratchet down once we have 2 weeks of data. We don’t have a good feel for variance yet.

Nadia Rahman: Agree. Also maybe extend evaluation window for tokens/sec to 30m (vs 20m) to smooth.

Sofia Ivanova: If we extend tokens/sec window, keep latency at 20m. Latency regressions are usually more immediate and less “averaged out”.

Tomáš Novák: Another pager fatigue angle: do we page per model? If 3 models regress from same runtime build, we’ll get 3 pages.

Sean Gallagher: Dedup idea 2: group alerts by {region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, metric, direction} and include top-N affected models in payload.
Downside: if model-specific regression, we might hide it.

Noah Patel: I’d still keep model in the key. Kernel selection can be model-specific. Grouping across models could obscure.

Allison Grant: Could do “alert grouping in PD” without changing the actual rule labels. I.e. use PD grouping key separate from metric label grouping.

Rafael Mendes: Yep. PD can group incidents by custom fields. We can set grouping = runtime_build + region + metric. Individual alerts still exist but you get one incident with multiple triggers.

Sean Gallagher: perfect. I’ll implement PD grouping like that.

Sean Gallagher: Concrete v0 changes based on thread:
- Paging thresholds:
  - p95 latency: +25% for 20m, min_samples>=250
  - tokens/sec: -25% for 30m, min_samples>=250
- Ticket thresholds unchanged for now (+15% / -10% over 60m)
- Deploy window behavior:
  - during deploy: ticket-only
  - post deploy end +10m: paging enabled
- Add “no data / label drop” separate alert (ticket) to telemetry queue
- PD grouping key: {runtime_build, region, metric}

Tomáš Novák: Looks good. Please add auto-resolve behavior? We’ve had incidents that stick around forever.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Auto-resolve when signal returns within 5% of baseline for 30m (and min_samples met) would help.

Nadia Rahman: Just make sure “returns to normal” uses the same baseline and doesn’t flip-flop. Maybe require 2 consecutive windows.

Sean Gallagher: ack. I’ll set resolve condition = regression < +5% (or > -5%) for 2 consecutive eval windows.

PagerDuty Bot: (test) Service "perf-canary-regressions" created by Rafael Mendes. Routing: eng-sre primary, eng-runtime secondary. Escalation: 15m to Runtime if unacked.

Marissa Cole: Can we ensure alert payload includes links: (1) perf-canary dashboard filtered to model/region (2) deploy diff (runtime SHA) (3) runbook.

Sean Gallagher: yup — wiring those into the payload is on the checklist. I’ll add to the alert template.

Noah Patel: Thanks. Once you’ve got the first week of pages/tickets, let’s do a quick review and recalibrate. We’ll probably end up with model-specific thresholds eventually.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. I’ll post the rule PR + PD config link here later today.
